evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 9.94 mg/L, well above 2.0 mg/L minimum; minimum observed was ~7.05 mg/L at 26.6 h with self-recovery
Receiving P at 48 h = 2.89 g/L matches source batches at 48 h (3.06, 3.02, 2.98 g/L); sources show continued production to ~8 g/L peak at 72-76 h
Receiving DO2 profile within/near source envelope throughout; no adverse divergence trend
Delayed assay clocks show P(t-4h) information pattern; receiving batch is in exponential production phase at decision time 52 h
args.rationale: Receiving batch is a normal case: DO2 ~10 mg/L (5x the 2 mg/L constraint floor), and the 48 h product assay (2.89 g/L) matches the source batches (2.98–3.06 g/L), which continued producing to ~8 g/L by 72–76 h. No oxygen risk, no feeding anomaly, and production is accelerating into its most productive window. Interventions (feed cuts, air changes, stop) would only reduce product mass or add needless energy; stop yields zero counted production. Keep is the bounded, lowest-risk choice.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters may differ from source; if the receiving process diverges after 52 h (e.g., faster feed exhaustion or hidden oxygen limitation later in the run), KEEP would miss a late-stage correction. However, all observables (DO2 margin, P alignment, trajectory shape) argue against this, and the transient DO2 dip at 24-27 h mirrored the source batches exactly. Moderate confidence in KEEP; monitor the next routine 60 h assay for confirmation.
